items.title: Harold Ousley interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: In fact we had a trumpet player on there named Frank, he played two trumpets at one time.

ctx.x: Now I read in something that you played for quite a number of years in a circus band.

Yeah, well that was only really not — it was only for one year — in fact not a whole year, for about four or five months. I joined a carnival, Haney Brothers. And I think I joined it in Champaign, Illinois. And of course the carnival plays cities, and usually on the outside or the outskirts of town. And they called that a still date. Because at that time it’s only the carnival there and it usually started say about six o’clock in the evening after people get off from work. And they’d come out on the carnival. And…

for that particular show would come out and he’d let the people know what they’re going to see. Well as soon as that show let out, if your tent was next then you had to be there to catch those people. And you’d bring them to your site. And of course when they got to us the barker would tell them — and then he would say a lot of things that was not true, like we got the girl that does the dance of the seven veils and she’d drop these veils one by one. Then the girl that does the dance with the balloons or bubbles…
